5.0.s.en: (1) Moses asks for the release of the people

5.0.0.en: With faith and courage Moses carried out the word of God, and he went in with Aaron to Pharaoh, and they asked him to let the people of Israel go to hold a feast to God in the wilderness and offer worship to Him. There are many opinions about the time of the exodus of the children of Israel from the land of Egypt and about the Pharaoh who was reigning at that time; most likely he was Rameses II, which means that their exodus was in the late thirteenth century BC.

5.1.0.en: With pride Pharaoh refused their words, despising the God of whom Moses was speaking.

5.2.0.en: Moses repeated his request, making clear that God had met him in the desert and had asked him to lead His people Israel on a three days' journey into the wilderness to worship Him there. He made clear the ability of this God to punish whoever opposes Him, for He could strike the people with pestilence or expose them to the attack of enemies and death by the sword.

5.3.0.en: Pharaoh accused Moses and Aaron of occupying the children of Israel with these strange ideas, which led to the disruption of work, and he rebuked them for that and commanded them to go to work and not be occupied with these strange ideas. But in rebuking them he commanded them to go to their burdens, and this is a clear admission from him that he was a tyrant and hard-hearted and put heavy works upon the children of Israel.

5.4.0.en: The people of the land: the children of Israel.

5.4.1.en: Pharaoh marveled at the request of Moses and Aaron, because despite the hard labor the children of Israel were doing, their number had greatly increased; how much more, then, if they rested from work, their numbers would increase and they would multiply more and more.

5.4.2.en: Do not be troubled if people object to your care for the worship of God or His service or to your encouraging others.. Bear with them and do not argue with them much, and hold fast to God, who rewards you and blesses your life.

5.5.s.en: (2) The burden of work is made heavier on the children of Israel

5.5.0.en: Taskmasters of the people: the Egyptian chiefs responsible on behalf of Pharaoh for the forced labor of the children of Israel.

5.5.1.en: Their officers: the Jewish chiefs responsible for leading the people in the work under the taskmasters. Pharaoh gathered the Egyptians responsible for employing the children of Israel and asked them not to give them straw to make bricks of mud, that is, raw bricks with which they build cities, but to let them go themselves to gather the straw from anywhere in Egypt. This of course required of the children of Israel greater effort and a longer time in the work.

5.6.0.en: Pharaoh also required the children of Israel to make the same quantity of bricks that they made every day to build the cities with. This was a punishment for them for trying to rest from work on the pretext of going out to worship God, accusing Moses and Aaron of spreading false words of no use, namely going out to worship God.

5.6.1.en: Do not be harsh in your treatment of others if they do not agree with you in your ideas, and do not hurry to judge them and condemn them, because God, who is stronger than all, watches you and will punish you if you persist in your harshness.

5.7.0.en: The Egyptian chiefs responsible for employing the children of Israel carried out Pharaoh's word and commanded them to gather the straw themselves and make the same quantity of mud bricks that was required of them every day.

5.8.s.en: (3) The children of Israel plead with Pharaoh

5.8.0.en: The children of Israel went out to look for stubble everywhere in Egypt to gather it so that they could make mud bricks with it, and their Egyptian chiefs urged them on to gather quickly and to work continuously so that they would make the same quantity required every day as was their custom.

5.9.0.en: The children of Israel were exerting great effort in making the quantities of mud bricks required of them every day, so when the gathering of straw was added to them as well, it became impossible to accomplish all this work. Pharaoh's cruelty appeared when the Egyptian taskmasters gathered the chiefs of the children of Israel and rebuked them for not completing what was required of them, and even beat them severely to frighten and humiliate them so that they would be harsh on their brethren to complete the enormous work required of them, even if it was beyond their strength or some of them fell dead from exhaustion; in this way Pharaoh would reduce their growing numbers.

5.10.1.en: The chiefs of the children of Israel went to Pharaoh pleading with him to lift from them this harsh ruling of gathering the straw or stubble needed to make mud bricks while still being bound to make the same quantity required of them every day, and they entreated him because they had done all they could and still were not able to complete what was required, and the Egyptian taskmasters beat them although they were wronged.

5.11.0.en: Pharaoh rejected the pleadings of the chiefs of the children of Israel and accused them of laziness, and that was why they asked him to go out to worship God, to escape completing their work. And he confirmed his decision that they should gather the stubble and make the same quantity of bricks.

5.11.1.en: Do not plead with the wicked, because they will not take pity on you, but plead with God, and He will have mercy on you and forgive you, whatever your sins or weaknesses or shortcomings.

5.12.s.en: (4) The children of Israel murmur against Moses

5.12.0.en: The chiefs of the children of Israel went out from Pharaoh in great distress after he had treated them harshly, and they found Moses and Aaron meeting them on the road, and they rebuked them severely for suggesting going out to worship God in the wilderness, the matter they had asked of Pharaoh, and because of which this injustice of gathering straw had come upon them; for this decision would lead to the death of many from exhaustion, so it would be like a sword by which many die.

5.13.0.en: Moses hurried to God and presented to Him the problem of his people, and even reproached Him because He had not delivered them but the injustice upon them had increased.

5.13.1.en: Place your problems before God, however difficult they are, confident of His love and His ability to do all things. God's speaking with Moses

6.0.0.en: God encouraged Moses that Pharaoh's opposition was temporary and would end, and that he would let the people of God go, and indeed would drive them out, that is, send them out quickly. This is what he did after the plague on the firstborn, when he was afraid and wanted to be rid of them because of his fear of their God.

6.0.1.en: God is able to change the hearts of the wicked so that they submit to you and do the will of God, so do not be disturbed by their threats or their wrongs, for they are temporary, and pray for them that they may return to God.

6.1.0.en: He declared that He is God, known to the fathers as the Lord Almighty. And here He adds to Moses His new name Jehovah, that is, the Existing One, and none other exists from eternity. The name Jehovah had been alluded to before, but not with such clarity (Gen 21:33). The Book of Genesis

6.2.0.en: He reminded Moses that He had promised them the inheritance of the land of Canaan and its possession, as mentioned in (Gen 12:2, 26:

6.2.1.en: 1-5, 46:3, 4), all this to remind him of His power and His promises so that his heart would be reassured in the face of Pharaoh's opposition and harshness.

6.3.0.en: I have remembered my covenant: I will fulfill my covenant, or the time has come to fulfill the covenant.

6.3.1.en: His tenderness is shown in hearing the prayers and the suffering of His people, as is His justice, since He sees the cruelty of the Egyptians and punishes them.

6.3.2.en: God is long-suffering toward those who wrong you, so do not doubt His tenderness, for He will surely save you; He is touched by all your pains and will not remain silent over the injustice that befalls you.

6.4.0.en: He asked him to proclaim to the children of Israel that God would save them with a mighty hand from the injustice of the Egyptians and their enslavement. This is the first mention of the word salvation, which was said here for deliverance from the slavery of Egypt and signifies deliverance from the slavery of sin by the redemption of Christ.

6.5.0.en: He declares His special fatherhood to His people; He is their own God and they are His beloved children.

6.5.1.en: And this declaration of His to the children of Israel that they were His people was because of their faith in Him at that time, while the rest of the peoples worshiped idols. This was a preparation for establishing a people who believe in Christ the Savior in the fullness of time, namely the Christians who believe in Him from all the countries of the world, while those of the Jews and the Gentiles who rejected Christ are not His people.

6.5.2.en: Enjoy the boldness of sonship and remind God of His promises when you need Him, and keep yourself pure so as to be a son worthy of God, and you will receive not only His rescue of you from afflictions but also the fellowship of His love, and you will become as if you were in heaven.

6.6.0.en: Which I did lift up my hand: that is, I swore.

6.6.1.en: I will give it you: I promised Abraham and his descendants its inheritance.

6.6.2.en: He confirmed to Moses His earlier promise to the fathers to give the land of Canaan as an inheritance to His people Israel if they remained firm in faith in Him and walked according to His commandments.

6.7.0.en: Moses spoke to the children of Israel all the words of God after his heart was comforted and strengthened by these divine promises, but the children of Israel did not have the faith that Moses had, so they did not believe him because of the humiliation they were enduring and the brokenness of their souls.

6.7.1.en: Beware lest the cares of the world keep you from hearing the voice of God, for they are temporary, and your God is able to reveal Himself in your life in the midst of afflictions. So do not give up your prayers and your readings, but seek God with persistence, and He will save you and lift your cares from you.

6.8.0.en: God commanded Moses to go in to Pharaoh a second time and ask him to let the people of God go to worship Him. This time he is not to ask permission for a journey of three days, but that they go out beyond the borders of Egypt.

6.9.0.en: Moses marveled at God's command, since the chiefs of his people had not listened to him and had not believed what he said, so how would Pharaoh accept his word. This was not from weakness of his faith in God for convincing Pharaoh, but from his sense of his personal weakness, that he was deficient and weak in expression and speech; so he attributed the children of Israel's not accepting his word to his weakness, and likewise expected Pharaoh to reject this word because he was of uncircumcised lips, that is, deficient in expression. And because the circumcised is a complete man, a son of God, while the uncircumcised signifies the distant, weak Gentiles, because of his weakness in speech he called himself of uncircumcised lips.

6.10.0.en: And gave them a charge: He strengthened them with words to say to the children of Israel and to Pharaoh.

6.10.1.en: God continued encouraging Moses and commanded him to go again to the children of Israel and assure them that God would save them, then go in to Pharaoh and demand of him the release of the people of God, and He gave him the words to say. The Book of Genesis

6.10.2.en: God is ready to give you a mouth and wisdom that will convince those who hear you, so ask Him, whatever your weakness, and He will strengthen you, and do not fear, however harsh or strong those you will meet may be, because your God is stronger than everyone in the world.

6.11.s.en: (3) The genealogy of Moses and Aaron

6.11.0.en: He mentioned the sons of Reuben and Simeon, who became chiefs of the clans. He began the sequence from the firstborn Reuben in order to reach Levi, who is the one meant, because he is the great-grandfather of Moses and Aaron. He mentioned the first three sons, who fell into grave sins: Reuben committed adultery with his father's wife during his father's lifetime, and Simeon and Levi killed the tribe of Hamor and Shechem. Here God shows His love in accepting sinners if they repent, for all of them are His children and He loves them despite their sins.

6.12.0.en: He mentioned the sons of Levi and their clans until he reached the mention of Amram, the father of Moses, who was one of the sons of Kohath. He makes clear that Levi, then his son Kohath, and after him his son Amram, lived long lives compared with those around them, to declare God's blessing upon them as a preparation for His great blessing upon their grandson Moses.

6.13.0.en: He declared the marriage of Amram to his father's sister Jochebed, which was permitted before the Law of Moses but was forbidden by the Law afterward (Lev 20:19). And he mentioned the children of Amram, Moses and Aaron, and did not mention here their sister Miriam because the discourse is about Moses and Aaron, who would lead the people.

6.14.0.en: He took care to mention the marriage of Aaron because he would be the high priest, and he married, though of the tribe of Levi, a wife from the tribe of Judah, the tribe from which Christ would come. He also mentioned a great person, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the grandson of Aaron, who was filled with zeal and killed the man who committed adultery with a foreign woman in violation of the Law of God (Num 25).

6.15.0.en: He makes clear that all the preceding genealogies were meant for Moses and Aaron, who would lead the people.

6.15.1.en: Take care of your lineage to God and the Church in which you were born through Baptism, for this is the source of your strength, and always remember that you are a child of God and His image, so you will walk in what pleases Him and reject the sin that angers Him, and you will be a light to the world and the salt of the earth.

7.0.0.en: A god: a lord and ruler.

7.0.1.en: Thy prophet: one speaking what you command him.

7.0.2.en: God granted Moses awesomeness in Pharaoh's sight through the strength of his personality and the plagues with which he would strike him, so that Pharaoh feared him and submitted and pleaded with him to save him, but unfortunately, because of the hardness of his heart, he would return and refuse to obey God.

7.0.3.en: God is able to give you awesomeness in the eyes of those around you, even if they object to you or oppose you, yet they feel a strange power in you, which is the power of God. So do not be disturbed by their wrongs, for they result from their anxiety and turmoil. Be strong and hold fast to God's commandments so that you declare His voice through your conduct and your words.

7.1.0.en: God commanded Moses to speak His words to Aaron, and Aaron to declare these words to Pharaoh. Thus Moses is humbled because he is unable to speak with Pharaoh, and Aaron is humbled because he is merely a spokesman of what Moses commands him.

7.1.1.en: Accept your incapacity, because it is the means of your salvation through humility before God and cooperation with those around you.

7.2.0.en: God declared to Moses that Pharaoh would refuse to hear his word, and God would allow the hardness of his heart and even use it to show His wonders by means of the ten plagues, so that the Egyptians would see the helplessness of their gods, that perhaps they might believe, and the children of Israel would be strengthened in the faith that their God is the God of gods.

7.3.0.en: That I may lay my hand: which calls me to punish and strike Egypt with many plagues.

7.3.1.en: Great judgments: I will judge them and pass sentence upon them and punish them with great plagues.

7.3.2.en: God declares His care for Israel, calling them His armies and His people, and therefore they are assured of His care and His deliverance of them from the humiliation and slavery of the Egyptians, so He strikes them to deliver His people from their hands.

7.4.0.en: God's purpose in the ten plagues is to call the Egyptians to faith, and not only to strengthen the faith of the children of Israel or of Moses and Aaron. Moses and Aaron believed the word of God and declared their readiness to carry out this word, and they were advanced in age, for they were over eighty years old.

7.5.s.en: (2) Moses' rod swallows up the rods of the magicians

7.5.0.en: Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and told him to let Israel go to worship God in the wilderness as God had commanded them, and he did not refuse their word outright, for Moses was given awesomeness. And Pharaoh asked him for a miracle to be sure that God had appeared to him. God had already instructed Moses to do the miracle of turning the rod into a serpent, so Moses cast down the rod, which is also called Aaron's rod, since Moses used to give his rod to Aaron to do the miracles with it, and it was also called "the rod of God" (ch. 4:20).

7.5.1.en: The rod signifies the Cross; as it accompanied Moses throughout his life, so also the Cross accompanies us throughout our lives, and by it we receive salvation through the sacraments of the Church. And the rod turned into a serpent because it signifies wisdom, the mother of virtues, by which we know our way to the Kingdom.

7.6.0.en: Pharaoh brought his magicians, who were led by two great magicians, "Jannes and Jambres"

7.6.1.en: (2 Tim 3:8). They did in like manner with their enchantments and cast down their rods, and they became serpents.

7.6.2.en: What the magicians did is the confusion and deception that the devil works on those who do not hold fast to the Church, showing powers and works that resemble the works of God, but by God's wisdom they are easily exposed.

7.7.0.en: The authority of God over Satan appeared when Aaron's rod swallowed up the rods of the magicians, that is, the serpent that came from Aaron's rod swallowed up the serpents of the magicians.

7.7.1.en: The power of God overcomes Satan in the end, so do not be disturbed by the powers of the world, and be patient until you see the power of God overcome and triumph in you, first by leaving sin, then He lifts the affliction and turns it into blessings in a way that surpasses understanding.

7.8.0.en: Pharaoh refused to believe in the power of God, the God of Moses, and also refused to let the children of Israel go from Egypt, because of his pride.

7.8.1.en: When God declares His voice to you, do not be stubborn with Him, led by the thoughts of your mind or your emotions, but regret what you have done and declare your apology to God and to those around you; in this you become strong because you are able to face yourself and return to the truth.

7.9.s.en: (3) Preparation for the plague of the river

7.9.0.en: God asked Moses to go the next morning to meet Pharaoh, who goes out to the River Nile; this going out may have been for a stroll, or for bathing, or for a religious festival. And He asked him to rebuke him for not letting the people of God go. Here God begins to show His authority through His prophet Moses, rebuking the wicked that perhaps they might repent. With this the ten plagues begin, by which God intended many benefits, the most important of which are:

7.9.1.en: 1- Showing the power of God, which is exalted above all the pagan gods spread in Egypt.

7.9.2.en: 2- God's support of the truth, His vindication of His wronged children and His punishment of the wrongdoers, that is, Pharaoh and all the Egyptians.

7.9.3.en: 3- Confirming the faith of the children of Israel that they worship the true God, so that they would despise the pagan gods.

7.9.4.en: 4- Confirming the power of His prophet Moses, whom He sent to bring His people out of Egypt, so that Pharaoh and all the Egyptians would fear him and all the children of Israel would also hold him in awe.

7.9.5.en: 5- Shattering the pagan Egyptian gods so that the Egyptians would believe in God and repent and return to Him; and this is indeed what happened, for some of them believed and joined the children of Israel, and they called them the mixed multitude.

7.9.6.en: There are different divisions of the ten plagues, since they included the pagan Egyptian gods and every power on which the Egyptians depended, and here is this division of the ten plagues:

7.9.7.en: 1- Harmful plagues in which the pagan gods become a source of weariness and distress for the Egyptians, such as turning the river into blood and the plague of frogs, gnats and flies.

7.9.8.en: 2- Plagues of diseases to prick the Egyptians so that they would repent, such as the plague of pestilence on the livestock and the boils on people and beasts.

7.9.9.en: 3- Plagues touching nature, in which God stirred up nature against the Egyptians, so the gods turned into enemies of the people, such as the plague of darkness, when the sun they worshiped disappeared, and the plague of hail accompanied by fire, when the beloved rain turned into hail and fire that killed them.

7.9.10.en: 4- The plague of insects, for He stirred up against them small insects such as the plague of locusts that ate all their good things.

7.9.11.en: 5- Man: and this is the hardest of the plagues, since it killed all the firstborn of Egypt.

7.9.12.en: If you have tested God through much prayer and the guidance of your father of confession, then carry out what He wants, however difficult, and do not draw back from carrying it out even if it is rebuking some great person or taking an action against the wishes of others.. Be obedient to God before people, and do not fear for yourself their harm or their words, because God will support you.

7.10.0.en: He commanded him to threaten Pharaoh that he would strike the River Nile with the rod and it would turn into blood, so that he would know that the God of the Hebrews is God alone and is above all the gods, among which is the River Nile, as the Egyptians worshiped it. The turning of water into blood signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who turns our striving from water to blood, that is, striving to the point of blood. The work of the Holy Spirit is sometimes gentle like water, then grows intense with power to remove every evil from us, even if we endure pains and torments that reach the shedding of blood.

7.11.0.en: He also threatened him that the fish would die and stink, and the Egyptians would not be able to drink the water or eat the fish, so they would be deprived of food and drink.

7.11.1.en: The hardness of your heart deprives you of God's material and spiritual blessings, so take care to obey Him and repent quickly of your sins.

7.12.s.en: (4) Turning the river into blood (the first plague)

7.12.0.en: Their streams: watering channels, that is, water canals.

7.12.1.en: In vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone: the wooden or stone basins in which water collects. Aaron struck the River Nile before Pharaoh, and all its waters along the length of the land of Egypt, with all the canals and branches going out from it, and also the ponds and all the gatherings of water (pools), turned into blood, so there was blood in all the canals, the streams and the basins for the crops.

7.13.0.en: The fish that lived in all the waters of Egypt also died and stank, and the Egyptians were unable to drink water from the Nile or from any of its branches or from the gatherings going out from it, and indeed its stench became troublesome to them.

7.13.1.en: The Fathers understood from this sign that the water turned into blood for the Egyptians only, while the children of Israel, when they took from the river, had water and not blood, so they drank in peace and did not need to dig wells to look for water as the Egyptians did in (v. 24). What perhaps led them to understand this is that the fourth plague, the plague of flies, was on the Egyptians only and not on the children of Israel (ch. 8:22-24); and likewise the plagues of boils, darkness and the firstborn; so they realized by this that all these ten plagues were on the Egyptians and not on the children of Israel.

7.14.0.en: Satan continued his confusion, and the magicians struck with their rods on gatherings of water, and they turned into blood; so Pharaoh refused to believe and submit to God or let his people go.

7.15.0.en: Pharaoh remained in his stubbornness as if the plague had not happened, and he neither returned to God nor let his people go.

7.15.1.en: Do not be stubborn with God and refuse to hear His voice, for every affliction that passes over you is a message from God to you to repent and do a spiritual work with Him.

7.16.0.en: The Egyptians were compelled to dig wells to drink from the groundwater, while the children of Israel did not need that, because the water of the Nile remained as it was and did not turn into blood for them. The plagues of frogs, gnats and flies
